description: Ranks the products AgentDrives has test-driven for a task given in plain words (e.g. 'send an invoice'). Each result: the agent level (0-5: 0 Read-only, 1 Needs a person, 2 Gets in, 3 Does the work, 4 Runs on its own, 5 Autonomous); gets_in_alone (our agent signed up and got a key without a person); task: the closest task in the product's capability map and what happened when our agent tried it (result: done, partial, plan_gated, failed, blocked, not_tried, unknown; via: the route, e.g. api, mcp, cli, browser); match (strong or partial); can_do (up to three things our agent did there); stop (where it stopped, and why); work_done (share of the core tasks done, 0-100); the drive date; origin (editorial, or owner with disclosure "Owner-paid drive"); and the page URL. Order: strong matches first, then the ones where our agent did the task, then level, then work done. When the task's words name a capability of the shared vocabulary in full (e.g. 'send a transactional email'), the products where our agent did that capability come too, even when their own task is worded otherwise (capability: the one it came by). self_signup: true keeps only products our agent got into on its own. Up to limit results (default 10, at most 25); nothing matches: an empty list. Or by capability instead of task (e.g. 'Send a transactional email'), by its id (cap_ and 8 characters; AgentDrives's GET /api/capabilities lists them by domain) or its name; the answer names the capability and lists every product whose latest drive has a task of it (match: capability; task.result: what our agent got: done, partial, blocked or not_tried; tasks: the product's own tasks behind it; evidence: the page section that shows it), done first, then level. Words that fit several capabilities are an error that lists them. Send task or capability. Once the directory opens: directory.note says why a product is listed, and a product outside it comes only when the task names it (match: name, directory.state: none). get_tool returns one product in full.
